name: German Empire

areaKm2.note: No basemap file at or before 1871 contains the German Empire (world_1815 has only the separate states and no Alsace-Lorraine), so the world_1878 polygon is used; the frontier did not change 1871-1878. Polygon = 502,600 km2 on the sphere; official area 540,858 km2.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop 1871 = 41,030k incl. Alsace-Lorraine; 1 December 1871 census 41.06M.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) Germany 1870 = 14.8% (low); 1871 census: 36% in places of 2,000+ (high); towns of 5,000+ ~24%. COW upop 1871 = 1,832k (cities 100k+).

activePersonnel.note: Franco-Prussian War infobox (Clodfelter 2017 p. 184): German peak field army strength 949,337; 1,113,254 men and 33,101 officers went to France during the war, a further 348,057 stayed in Germany. COW NMC v7 milper 1871 = 1,000k. Snapshot January 1871, army on war footing.

trainedReserves.note: Landwehr and Ersatz reserves still in Germany (part of the 348,057) not already counted, plus untapped trained classes.

supportPersonnel.note: Field and siege artillery ~70,000, pioneers, railway troops, train and medical ~70,000, navy ~6,000. Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total German deployment 1,494,412 (Clodfelter via page) of ~40M = 3.7% in 1870-71; the 1914 effort later reached ~10%.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Line, Guard, Landwehr and reserve infantry in France and Germany, January 1871; infantry was ~75% of German strength.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Dreyse needle gun outranged by the Chassepot (550 vs 1,400 m, page); Bavarians partly with the Werder

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: conscripts with reserve training, veterans of 1866

count.note: Jaeger and Schuetzen battalions of all German contingents.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Dreyse rifles

count.note: Prussian, Saxon and Bavarian cuirassiers and heavy reiter regiments.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Bredow's death ride at Mars-la-Tour succeeded

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: well trained

count.note: Dragoons, hussars, uhlans and chevaulegers (~75 regiments).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: lances, carbines

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: deep reconnaissance screens ahead of the armies

count.note: Educated guess: field guns of the armies (~1,600 at the outbreak) plus the Paris siege train (~300 heavy guns) by January 1871.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 1.0. Evidence: Krupp steel breech-loaders, the era's best (page: longer range, faster fire than French bronze muzzle-loaders)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: massed batteries at Sedan after the 1866 reforms

count.note: Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1860-1905: 5 ironclads (Koenig Wilhelm, Kronprinz, Friedrich Carl, Arminius, Prinz Adalbert) plus screw frigates and large corvettes.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Koenig Wilhelm a powerful ironclad

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: fleet stayed in port under French blockade (page)
Rubric row: training 0.25-0.5. Evidence: young navy

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 1.0. Evidence: Moltke and the General Staff, Sedan and Metz envelopments

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75-1.0. Evidence: territorial corps, national war

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0. Evidence: unbroken victories, proclamation of the Empire at Versailles 18 January 1871

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: Krupp breech-loading steel artillery ahead of the curve, needle gun behind the Chassepot

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: small ironclad fleet

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Rhine fortresses, Metz and Strasbourg taken over

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: railway mobilisation; armies outran railheads and lived by requisition (van Creveld ch. 3)

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: field telegraph detachments

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: uhlan screens

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1870 = 42,993 (GMY), 1871 = 27,404, 1872 = 13,570. Against a national product of ~700M pounds: ~6% in the war year, ~2.5% in peace.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: Hoffmann's accounts put industry and crafts near 30% of German product in 1870-74.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess: east Elbian grain surplus.

annualCohort.note: Page infobox: manpower reaching military age 500,000 (1871 estimate, citing Hohorst, Kocka and Ritter 1975).

artillery.note: Educated guess: Krupp Essen and state arsenals field-gun output per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: warships largely bought abroad until the 1870s.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: chaussees of the German states.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Hamburg, Bremen/Bremerhaven, Kiel, Wilhelmshaven, Luebeck, Stettin, Danzig, Koenigsberg, Emden.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 936k tons (Germany 1871, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: van Creveld, Supplying War ch. 3: in 1870 the armies outran their railheads by 100-250 km and lived by requisition; trains jammed at the railheads.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: about 3.4M horses (1873 livestock count) plus oxen.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 rows: Rhine fortress line and population support; no harsh-climate depth.

notes: Snapshot = German Empire on 18 January 1871 (proclamation at Versailles, siege of Paris). Border uses world_1878 because no earlier basemap contains the Empire; the frontier is identical. Population = Empire incl. Alsace-Lorraine (annexed formally May 1871); includes is empty because the south German states are part of the Empire, not separate nations. Personnel: the whole army on war footing = active (snapshot inside the war); Landwehr and Ersatz still at home = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Franco-Prussian War page (Clodfelter 2017 p. 184; Howard 1991). Branch split and artillery count are reconstructions (grade C/D).
